The parameter draws behind a prediction

Source: R/ilm_extend.R, R/zzz-iml-aliases.R
ilm_predict_draws.Rd

ilm_predict_draws() is the step of ilm_predict() that draws the model's parameters. Every prediction, forecast, score, calibration and cross-validation in limn is computed from these draws. You will not normally call it yourself: it is a generic, so that a package fitting illume's models another way can supply the draws from its own fits, and limn then works on those fits unchanged.

Usage

ilm_predict_draws(fit, nsim, seed, uncertainty, natural, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ilm_model'
ilm_predict_draws(fit, nsim, seed, uncertainty, natural, ...)

Arguments

fit

A fitted model: an "ilm_model", or a class that inherits from it.

nsim

The number of draws to return.

seed

The seed the draws are made from. The same seed must give the same draws, whatever else is running.

uncertainty

Which parameters are drawn, as in ilm_predict(): "joint" (all of them), "fixed" (the variances held at their estimates), "latent" (every parameter held, so only the random effects and latent cells are drawn) or "none" (one draw, at the estimates). A method may refuse a value it has no meaning for, with an error that says which values it supports.

natural

Whether each draw's variances are also needed on their natural scale. limn asks for them only when a unit's effects are drawn afresh or averaged over.

...

Passed on to methods.

Value

An object of class "ilm_draws", as illume::ilm_draws() returns:

  • draws: a matrix with one row per parameter, in illume's order and on its internal scale, and nsim columns (one for uncertainty = "none");

  • mode: the estimates;

  • map: what each row of draws is, as illume::ilm_draws() gives it;

  • natural: when natural = TRUE, each draw's variances on their natural scale, which at the estimates equal illume::ilm_varcorr()'s.

ilm_predict() checks this shape, and stops with a message saying what is wrong when a method returns something else.

Details

The method for illume's fits draws from the fit's normal approximation, with illume::ilm_draws(). A method for another class of fit must return the same shape: the class of fit must inherit from "ilm_model", so that illume's illume::ilm_dist(), illume::ilm_varcorr(), illume::ilm_matrices() and illume::ilm_cells() accept it, and the draws must be laid out as illume::ilm_draws() lays them out.

Checks

What each check means and what to do about it, in the words it is printed with. A reference supports what was found and why; a remedy draws on it only where it says so, and anything marked as limn's own reasoning is not the source's:

  • parameter draws (fail): The parameter draws for this fit are not in the shape limn needs: what is wrong. Every prediction is computed from the draws ilm_predict_draws() returns, laid out as illume::ilm_draws() lays them out. The method for this class of fit returned something else. If the fit's class comes from another package, its ilm_predict_draws() method needs fixing there: ?ilm_predict_draws gives the shape. For an illume fit this is a fault in limn; please report it.

See also

ilm_cv_refit(), the other extension point.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(g = factor(rep(letters[1:8], each = 5)), x = rnorm(40))
d$y <- rpois(40, exp(0.5 + 0.3 * d$x))
fit <- illume::ilm_model(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = d, family = "poisson",
                         verbose = FALSE)
#> ilm_model(): the random-effect covariance of `g` sits at the edge of its range -- a variance of zero or a correlation of +/-1 -- where the data cannot resolve it. The fixed effects and their standard errors are still usable; summary() says what else is. If the term belongs in the model, boundary = "avoid" keeps it inside its range with a small penalty: it is then assumed nonzero rather than estimated at zero, so do not test whether it is; its variance comes out larger, and for a binary or categorical outcome the fixed effects a little further from zero -- markedly so when a category is rare.
dr <- ilm_predict_draws(fit, nsim = 10, seed = 1, uncertainty = "joint",
                        natural = FALSE)
dim(dr$draws)
#> [1] 11 10
